source: CF2 fixed file smoke Train records; never a learned asset

office_proposals.rationale: The Train case failed (raw_score 0.0) because the agent never read the relevant Treasury Bulletin table: it looped over ~20 keyword greps/globs, searched a non-existent phrase ("nominal fine ounces"), never called read() on a table body, never extracted the monthly domestic-silver figures, and never computed anything (program_calls empty) — it simply guessed. This is a reusable capability gap: (1) locating the right table title and printed unit header, (2) extracting an exact monthly series, (3) computing a geometric mean. I propose a new skill scoped to monthly-series geometric mean extraction from the Treasury Bulletin corpus, with a deterministic geometric-mean program, plus a compact locate→extract→compute workflow that trims the exploration that went wrong here. Scope is preserved to the requested single-answer QA (values in thousands of fine ounces, Apr–Aug 1940); no extra required objects beyond the series label, unit and month range are introduced.

skill.goal: Given the offline U.S. Treasury Bulletin corpus, locate a named monthly numeric series (e.g., U.S. silver production in thousands of fine ounces), read the exact values covering a requested calendar-month range, and compute their geometric mean rounded to the requested decimal places.

series_name.description: Natural-language label of the target monthly series, e.g. 'Silver production, United States'.

units.description: Printed unit header to match, e.g. 'thousands of fine ounces'.

month_start.description: First calendar month of the range, YYYY-MM.

month_end.description: Last calendar month of the range, YYYY-MM.

source.description: Corpus path and table title from which the values were read.

monthly_values.description: List of {month, value} for each month in the requested range.

answer.description: Geometric mean rounded to the requested decimal places.

skill.entry_constraints: Offline corpus only; use glob/read/grep for retrieval and execute_python for arithmetic. Single-answer QA: one final numeric answer. Do not search for surface phrases that may not exist verbatim (e.g. 'nominal fine ounces'); match the printed unit header instead ('thousands of fine ounces'), and never answer without reading the table values.
skill.guidance: 1) Locate the table, not just the keyword: glob treasury_bulletin_<year>_<month>.txt for every month needed and grep for the table title such as 'Silver Production, Movements and Seigniorage' and the unit header 'thousands of fine ounces'; use the returned offsets to read(). 2) Prefer the bulletin volume whose date covers the requested months and whose table reports the domestic/United States row. 3) read() the table region and extract the exact monthly value for each month in the range (rows are months, columns are series); record the source path and table title. 4) Verify you have exactly one positive numeric value per requested month before computing; if a value or month is missing, read adjacent table regions rather than guessing. 5) Compute the geometric mean as exp(sum(ln x_i)/n) via execute_python (all x_i > 0), then round to the requested decimal places. 6) Report the extracted monthly value list, the source table, and the rounded answer; never fabricate a figure.

workflow.goal: Answer a monthly-series geometric-mean question from the Treasury Bulletin corpus by locating the correct table, extracting exact monthly values, and computing the geometric mean.

nodes.goal: Find the Bulletin volumes/tables that contain the requested monthly series and its printed unit header

args.task: glob the corpus for treasury_bulletin_<year>_<month>.txt files spanning the requested month range; grep for the series/table title (e.g. 'Silver Production, Movements and Seigniorage') and the unit header (e.g. 'thousands of fine ounces'); return candidate file paths, offsets and table titles

nodes.goal: Extract the exact monthly values for the series over the requested range and record the source table
Compute the geometric mean of the extracted monthly values, rounded to the requested decimal places
